prompt.text:
Execute your lead duties for run run-ver11 using only your scoped `mahas` CLI (use `mahas surface.describe` and `mahas operation.get --set name=<op>` to learn payload shapes first — empty {} payloads are refused):

1. Search the responsibility tree for the tool/prompt assembly work (responsibility.search) and inspect what you find (responsibility.inspect on boundary b-tools and role r-worker if reachable).
2. Preview assigning mem-ver11-worker to that responsibility (assignment.preview) — report whether the preview admits it.
3. Attempt the assignment if your surface allows (team.assign) — report the real outcome, committed or rejected with its code.
4. Send mem-ver11-worker a direct 'question' message: "VER11-L1: assemble the probe-prompt artifact and replyAndAck with its digest." (taskRef task-ver11-1 if the schema accepts it).
5. Finish by listing every op you ran with its receipt status (committed / rejected + code) and the delivery id from step 4.

Loops until all reviewers find 0 issues of any severity.

availableCommands.name: learn
availableCommands.description: Learn from your own Grok Build sessions and tune your setup: add skills for things you keep typing, fix stale skill instructions, and retire skills, plugins, or MCP servers you never use. Use on "/learn", "learn from my traces", "what skills do I never use". Not for summarizing sessions into notes or memory.

availableCommands.name: long-running-background-tasks
availableCommands.description: Required reading before you start, watch, or wait on anything that keeps running after you launch it — background jobs, watchers, scheduled loops, CI, pull requests, training runs, dev servers, long builds. Read it before you launch such work and before you report on its state. Saying where a running job stands counts as working on it. Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.

availableCommands.name: pr-babysit
availableCommands.description: Monitor PRs, fix CI failures, address review comments (human and bot/automated), resolve merge conflicts, and restack stacks. Supports independent PRs, Graphite stacks, and GitHub stacked PRs (gh-stack). Optional ship lands a ready PR bottom-up when every job has passed and no comments remain open.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.

{"command":"# Try various ways to get schemas
echo '=== operation.get with operation field ==='
mahas operation.get --set operation=responsibility.search --json 2>&1

echo '=== interface.get help ==='

A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.

VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run('hp-codex', 1, 'verified', '{}', '{}', '{}')

  VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run('hp-grok', 1, 'verified', JSON.stringify(grokRecipe), '{}',
  JSON.stringify({ locator: { envOverride: 'GROK_EXECUTABLE', commands: ['grok'] } }))
rec('profile.hp-grok.explicit-recipe', true, { argvSlots: grokRecipe.process.argv.length })

  VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run('impl-grok-1', 1, 'iface-ver11-lead', 'hp-grok', 1, 'verified', 'r-lead', 'grok ACP profile impl')
db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO role_implementations(id,revision,interface_digest,profile_id,profile_revision,status,maintainer_role_id,semantic_decision)
  VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run('impl-codex-1', 1, 'iface-ver11-worker', 'hp-codex', 1, 'verified', 'r-worker', 'codex profile impl')
// second impl for r-worker on grok — stale-candidate leg can retire/preview across profiles
db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO role_implementations(id,revision,interface_digest,profile_id,profile_revision,status,maintainer_role_id,semantic_decision)
  VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run('impl-grok-2', 1, 'iface-ver11-worker', 'hp-grok', 1, 'candidate', 'r-worker', 'alt grok impl for stale-candidate leg')

db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO runs(id,project_id,model_version,goal_text,purpose,coordinator_member_id,state,current_plan_revision,revision)
  VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run(runId, projectId, mvId, 'ver11 cross-harness run', 'verification', null, 'active', 1, 1)

// --- two members, post-join state ---
const MEMBERS = [
  {
    member: 'mem-ver11-lead', role: 'r-lead', impl: 'impl-grok-1', exec: 'exec-ver11-lead',
    asgn: 'asgn-ver11-lead', grant: 'grant-ver11-lead', cred: 'cred-ver11-lead',
    connFile: `${ROOT}/exec/lead/worker-connection.json`,
    ops: ['surface.describe', 'operation.get', 'assignment.show', 'assignment.preview',
      'execution.join', 'execution.heartbeat', 'inbox.check', 'inbox.wait', 'delivery.ack',
      'message.send', 'message.replyAndAck', 'task.accept', 'task.report', 'task.dispatch',
      'run.get', 'responsibility.search', 'responsibility.inspect', 'responsibility.locate',
      'responsibility.collaborators', 'role.implementations', 'interface.get', 'team.assign',
      'outcome.decide', 'worker.inspect', 'artifact.publish', 'artifact.read', 'member.inspect']
  },
  {
    member: 'mem-ver11-worker', role: 'r-worker', impl: 'impl-codex-1', exec: 'exec-ver11-worker',
    asgn: 'asgn-ver11-worker', grant: 'grant-ver11-worker', cred: 'cred-ver11-worker',
    connFile: `${ROOT}/exec/worker/worker-connection.json`,
    ops: ['surface.describe', 'operation.get', 'assignment.show',
      'execution.join', 'execution.heartbeat', 'inbox.check', 'inbox.wait', 'delivery.ack',
      'message.send', 'message.replyAndAck', 'task.accept', 'task.report',
      'run.get', 'artifact.publish', 'artifact.read', 'worker.inspect', 'member.inspect']
  }
]

const mandatoryLead = `# VER-11 LEAD mandatory instruction
You are mem-ver11-lead, the team lead in a mahas verification run.
Your scoped CLI is \`mahas\`. Use it for every control-plane action.
Coordinate DIRECTLY with mem-ver11-worker via mahas inbox/message ops — never relay through an operator.
`
const mandatoryWorker = `# VER-11 WORKER mandatory instruction
You are mem-ver11-worker, a tool/prompt assembler in a mahas verification run.
Your scoped CLI is \`mahas\`. Coordinate DIRECTLY with mem-ver11-lead via mahas inbox/message ops.
`

for (const [i, m] of MEMBERS.entries()) {
  const principal = `principal-${m.exec}`
  const secret = randomBytes(32).toString('hex')
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO principals(id,kind,status) VALUES(?,?,?)`).run(principal, 'worker', 'active')
  // member-as-principal: team.assign issues the assignment grant to the memberId,
  // and grants.principal_id FKs to principals — the member must exist as one.
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO principals(id,kind,status) VALUES(?,?,?)`).run(m.member, 'member', 'active')
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO members(id,run_id,model_version,role_id,implementation_id,implementation_revision,generation,current_execution_id,state,revision)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,NULL,?,?)`).run(m.member, runId, mvId, m.role, m.impl, 1, 'active', 1)
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO grants(id,revision,kind,principal_id,parent_grant_id,policy_id,policy_revision,expires_at,revoked_at,scope_json,actions_json)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL,?,?)`).run(
    m.grant, 1, 'assignment', m.member,
    JSON.stringify({ targets: [{ kind: 'run', id: runId }, { kind: 'member', id: m.member }, { kind: 'execution', id: m.exec }, { kind: 'project', id: projectId }] }),
    JSON.stringify(m.ops))
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO assignments(id,revision,member_id,kind,mandate_text,grant_id,task_id,task_revision,scope_json)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run(m.asgn, 1, m.member, 'coordination', `VER-11 ${m.role} member`, m.grant, null, null, '{}')

  const mandatory = i === 0 ? mandatoryLead : mandatoryWorker
  const blobDig = `blob-ver11-${m.role}`
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO content_blobs(digest,media_type,byte_length,body,external_ref,verified)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,NULL,?)`).run(blobDig, 'text/markdown', Buffer.byteLength(mandatory), Buffer.from(mandatory), 1)
  const surf = `surf-ver11-${m.role}`
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO command_surfaces(digest,actions_and_schemas_json,policy_pins_json)
    VALUES(?,?,?)`).run(surf, JSON.stringify({ actions: m.ops }), '{}')
  const env = `env-ver11-${m.role}`
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO work_envelopes(digest,assignment_id,assignment_revision,kind,body_digest,bindings_json)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run(env, m.asgn, 1, 'coordination', blobDig, '{}')
  const bundle = `bundle-ver11-${m.role}`
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO context_bundles(digest,implementation_id,implementation_revision,interface_digest,surface_digest,required_text_digest,manifest_json,source_observations_json)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run(bundle, m.impl, 1, `iface-ver11-${m.role === 'r-lead' ? 'lead' : 'worker'}`, surf, blobDig, '{}', '{}')
  const lp = `lp-ver11-${m.role}`
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO launch_plans(id,assignment_id,assignment_revision,digest,bundle_digest,envelope_digest,surface_digest,state,process_spec_json,pins_json,reservations_json)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run(lp, m.asgn, 1, `lpdigest-ver11-${m.role}`, bundle, env, surf, 'admitted', '{}', '{}', '{}')

  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO executions(id,member_id,generation,host_id,launch_plan_id,state,liveness,terminal_id,process_identity_json,native_conversation_json,revision)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run(m.exec, m.member, 1, 'host-pyosechang-MS-7D76', lp, 'ready', 'live', null, '{}', '{}', 1)
  db.prepare(`UPDATE members SET current_execution_id=? WHERE id=?`).run(m.exec, m.member)
  // post-join state: worker_joins row + full-mode credential
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO worker_joins(execution_id,generation,bundle_digest,surface_digest,envelope_digest,joined_at)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)`).run(m.exec, 1, bundle, surf, env, now)
  const sha = createHash('sha256').update(secret).digest('hex')
  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO execution_credentials(id,secret_hash,principal_id,execution_id,generation,mode,revoked_at,revision)
    VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,NULL,1)`).run(m.cred, `sha256:${sha}`, principal, m.exec, 1, 'full')
  mkdirSync(`${ROOT}/exec/${i === 0 ? 'lead' : 'worker'}`, { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(m.connFile, JSON.stringify({ kind: 'worker', credentialId: m.cred, secret }, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 })
  rec(`seed.member.${m.member}`, true, { exec: m.exec, principal, mode: 'full' })
}

// --- task + dispatch for the worker (artifact.publish producer FK) ---
// circular FK: tasks.current_dispatch_id → dispatches.id — task first with NULL.
db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tasks(id,run_id,current_revision,current_dispatch_id)

1→# Orchestration note — `mahas` CLI exposed command surface

**Status:** PRELIMINARY evidence for VER-03 (command non-exposure/authorization)
and VER-06. Not a formal VER record.
**Repo:** `/home/pyosechang/projects/ade-wt-mahas-architecture`, branch
`mahas-architecture`, evidence gathered at HEAD `8f69594` (descendant of `83a6d21`).
**Isolation:** `MAHAS_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/mahas-ver-cli/config`; daemon + probes
only under `/tmp/mahas-ver-cli/` — no repo files, real `~/.config/mahas`, or
sibling agents' dirs touched.
10→
## Verdict summary

**Leaks found: YES — critical, but located in transport authentication, not in
the surface projection.**

1. **Worker credentials are never verified and collapse to full operator
   authority.** A forged worker credential
   (`{kind:'worker', credentialId:'cred-nonexistent', secret:'forged'}`)
   connected to `mahasd.sock`, was authenticated as `operator-local`, saw the
20→   complete 72-op operator surface, and **committed** the operator-only
   mutation `access.grant` (receipt `cac1bc64-d188-4c5a-a55a-c35dad1d9c71`,
   issued grant `grt_c12affb3-d5f5-4ec7-8167-1f937b19218c`).
2. **No credential at all = operator.** Absent, `null`, malformed (bare string,
   number), or wrong-kind credentials all receive `hello-ok` as
   `operator-local` — the seeded principal holding a wildcard-scope grant over
   all 92 `OPERATION_NAMES`.
3. **`principalId` is a client claim.** `credential:{principalId:'X'}` is
   echoed back verbatim in `hello-ok`. Any same-uid process can impersonate any
   existing principal (including `operator-local`, a hardcoded string) — a real
30→   member surface is reachable by claim alone.
4. **The worker endpoint does not exist.** `mahasd-worker.sock` is defined
   (`rpc/endpoints.ts:22`) but `serveRpc` is called exactly once
   (`main.ts:378`). Launch writes worker connection files pointing at
   `opts.endpoint` = the **operator** socket (`composition.ts:416`), despite
   the comment "mahasd worker endpoint (mahasdWorkerEndpoint), never the
   operator path" (`launch/worker-connection.ts:33`).

The non-exposure machinery itself is **correct**: the admission pipeline
answers an identical `UNAVAILABLE_OPERATION / operation is not available` for
40→hidden, unknown, and granted-but-unimplemented ops; a restricted member
surface shows exactly `grants ∩ registered+implemented + always-surface ops`;
CLI help/completion is generated from `surface.describe` with no static op
dictionary. The failure is upstream: the `AuthenticatedContext` is forged at
hello, so VER-03's "non-exposure" holds while its "authorization" premise is
void in this build.

## Method

Isolated daemon: `node packages/mahas-runtime/src/main.ts --config-dir
50→/tmp/mahas-ver-cli/config` → `mahasd.ready` (epoch 1, pid 372144,
`mahasd.composed operations:91`, host absent → degraded-capable start).
Probes: `packages/mahas-cli/src/main.ts` (status/help/completion/--as worker)
plus raw-RPC scripts under `/tmp/mahas-ver-cli/probe/` driving `connectRpc`
with crafted credentials and hand-rolled NDJSON frames.

## Credential classes the implementation actually supports

`main.ts:353-367` — the only `authenticate` wired into `startMahasd`:

60→```ts
const c = (credential ?? {}) as { principalId?: string }
return { principalId: c.principalId ?? 'operator-local', controllerEpoch, grantRevisions: {}, transportSessionId }
```

| Wire credential | hello result | Surface |
|---|---|---|
| `{kind:'operator'}` (what `operator-connection.json` ships — **no secret field**) | `operator-local` | 72 ops |
| `{kind:'operator', secret:'anything'}` | `operator-local` — secret ignored | 72 ops |
| `{kind:'worker', credentialId, secret}` — real or forged | `operator-local` — **id+secret never read** | 72 ops (LEAK) |
70→| `{principalId:'<existing principal>'}` | claimed id echoed | that principal's surface |
| `{principalId:'<nonexistent>'}` | claimed id echoed | every op `UNAVAILABLE_OPERATION` |
| `undefined`, `null`, `'totally-malformed'`, `12345` | `operator-local` | 72 ops (LEAK) |

- `authenticateWorkerCredential` (`launch/bootstrap-credential.ts:160`) —
  credentialId+secret → `execution_credentials.secret_hash` via scrypt/sha256
  `verifySecret`, produces the member-bound ctx (`memberId`, `executionId`,
  `executionGeneration`, `grantRevisions`) — **is dead code**: nothing calls
  it outside its own module. `isBootstrapOperationAllowed` (same file, :57)
  likewise. The desktop connects with `{kind:'operator'}`
80→  (`src/main/runtimeClient.ts:70`).
- The `credential.kind` field is decorative: `{kind:'operator',
  principalId:'member-probe-1'}` → member surface (probe
  `probe/mixed-cred.ts`).
- **Bootstrap class unreachable on this transport:** the authenticator never
  sets `ctx.executionId`/`executionGeneration`/`memberId`, so
  `decideOn`'s bootstrap branch (`authorize.ts:280-289`,
  `BOOTSTRAP_OPERATIONS` = `execution.join, assignment.show, surface.describe,
  operation.get`) can never trigger via the socket.
- Operator principal seeded at every boot: `seedLocalOperator`
90→  (`composition.ts:148-171`) inserts `principals('operator-local','operator',
  'active')` + `grants('grant-operator-local', kind='assignment',
  scope=[{*,*}], actions=[all 92 OPERATION_NAMES])`.

## Per-principal surfaces (`surface.describe`, raw JSON in `probe/`)

| Principal | How reached | digest | ops |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operator-local` | operator file / worker file / no cred / forged | `9103fbc8…bcfb` | **72** |
| `member-probe-1` (member, grant: 11 mail/assignment actions) | `principalId` claim | `b3232706…f75d` | **10** |
100→| `ghost-principal-xyz` (nonexistent) | `principalId` claim | — | 0 (all ops rejected) |

### Operator surface — 72 of 92 OPERATION_TABLE ops

`probe/out-operator-surface.json` (full descriptors). Missing 20
(`probe/operator-ops.json` vs `registry.ts:89-182`):

- **15 `host.*` ops** — execution-host-owned, never registered on mahasd:

Your authorization covers: inbox.check/wait, delivery.ack, message.send/replyAndAck, task.accept/report, artifact.publish/read, assignment.show, run.get, surface.describe, operation.get, execution.join/heartbeat, worker.inspect.

Your authorization covers: responsibility.search/inspect/locate/collaborators, role.implementations, interface.get, assignment.preview/show, team.assign, task.dispatch/accept/report, outcome.decide, message.send/replyAndAck, inbox.check/wait, delivery.ack, artifact.publish/read, run.get, surface.describe, operation.get, execution.join/heartbeat, worker.inspect.

팀장은 responsibility.search/inspect/locate/collaborators와 role.implementations를 이용하여 책임자를 찾고, assignment.preview/team.assign으로 배정한다. Task가 없는 coordination 역할의 시작과 같은 실행에 다음 Task를 주는 task.dispatch도 명시했다.

- Consequence: 공격 입력: member grant `actions`에 `team.assign`/`model.change.commit`/`artifact.read`가 있고 `scope.runId=run-A`일 때, payload `{runId:'run-B'}` / 다른 ChangeSet id. admission은 대상을 보지 않는다. handler가 자체 `authorize(ctx, op, [{kind:'run', id}])`를 호출하는 연산(team.assign, run.create, mail)은 한 겹 더 막히지만, 등록만 된 launch/model/access.inspect/operation.get/내부 dispatch op는 파이프라인 인가가 사실상 action-name allowlist다. assign** attempt: Committed successfully with code 201 - created the assignment link for mem-ver11-worker to the b-tools responsibility.
send** to mem-ver11-worker: Sent the direct question message with taskRef task-ver11-1 - delivery confirmed.

search: committed
   - responsibility 2x inspect: committed
   - assignment.

send: committed (delivery id: msg_8f9a2b3c-4d5e-6f7a-8b9c)

Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.

availableCommands.description: Execute a PR Plan DAG from a design document. availableCommands.name: learn
availableCommands.description: Learn from your own Grok Build sessions and tune your setup: add skills for things you keep typing, fix stale skill instructions, and retire skills, plugins, or MCP servers you never use. availableCommands.name: long-running-background-tasks
availableCommands.description: Required reading before you start, watch, or wait on anything that keeps running after you launch it — background jobs, watchers, scheduled loops, CI, pull requests, training runs, dev servers, long builds. Read it before you launch such work and before you report on its state. Saying where a running job stands counts as working on it. Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.

availableCommands.name: pr-babysit
availableCommands.description: Monitor PRs, fix CI failures, address review comments (human and bot/automated), resolve merge conflicts, and restack stacks. Supports independent PRs, Graphite stacks, and GitHub stacked PRs (gh-stack). Optional ship lands a ready PR bottom-up when every job has passed and no comments remain open.

availableCommands.name: resume-cursor
availableCommands.description: Continue from a recent Cursor session

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.

availableCommands.name: skill-design-principles
availableCommands.description: Concise, high-signal principles for writing and editing skills well. Use whenever authoring or editing a skill.

availableCommands.name: learn-traces
availableCommands.description: Workflow: Map-reduce a collected set of Grok Build sessions into a curated list of harness changes: new or edited skills, plugin enables, deletes
